The dry gallery is the half of Kestrel Deep that people live in: two hundred metres of bored
ice, sealed and pressurised, with the cap and the slot board at one end and the soak lock at
the other. Forty members sleep, eat, argue and are paid along it. The exchanger trunks run
the whole length at shoulder height, hot to the hand, and they are the reason the gallery is
habitable and the reason it smells of scorched brass in the last hour before a shift change.

Overhead, always, the shelf. It is not heard so much as felt through the floor, a slow
working that the long-service members can date a calving by. Nobody looks up. Everybody
knows what is up there.

The slot board hangs at the cap end, and it is where the co-op becomes a physical object.
Soak slots, rotations, indemnity notices and, at present, the sealing order are pinned to it
in the steward's hand. A person who cannot get a line on that board cannot go anywhere, and
there is only one anywhere to go: the soak lock at the deep end, six hours of cold soak, and
the vault.

A note for whoever reads this tree. Locations are hierarchical and a scene's `location` is
normally a leaf, but this installation has exactly two records and the root is inhabited.
`kestrel_deep` is both the parent of `pump_vault` and the place a character stands when they
are not in the vault. Scenes set here are not a violation of the convention; there is simply
nothing below this level worth its own record.
